title: Crêpes Suzette
subtitle: French pancakes in caramelised orange butter with Grand Marnier
excerpt: Thin French crêpes folded and reheated in a buttery caramelised orange and Grand Marnier sauce, flambéed at the table. An old-school French dessert of genuine drama and exceptional flavour.

recipe.sourceNotes: Crêpes Suzette is a French dessert with a famous (and probably largely invented) origin story involving the future King Edward VII and a young waiter named Henri Charpentier who accidentally set fire to the sauce. The dish is associated with the Belle Époque era and the theatre of tableside cooking in grand French restaurants. The essential components are a crêpe batter made with butter and orange zest, and a caramelised butter and orange sauce flambéed with Grand Marnier or Cointreau. The flambé is theatrical but optional: the alcohol cooks off completely and the flavour is the same without it, just less spectacular.

recipeTools.notes: A 20 to 22 cm crêpe pan or non-stick frying pan.

content.text: Rest the crêpe batter for at least 30 minutes before cooking: this lets the gluten relax so the crêpes roll out thin and even. The first crêpe almost always goes wrong as the pan finds its temperature: set it aside for the cook to eat. Each crêpe should be very thin and lightly golden with darker spots. For the sauce, the butter and sugar must properly caramelise before the orange juice goes in: the caramel note is as important as the orange.
Make the batter: whisk the flour, eggs, milk, melted butter, orange zest, and sugar together until completely smooth. Rest for 30 minutes.

Cook the crêpes: heat a 20 cm pan over medium-high heat and brush with a little oil. Pour in just enough batter to coat the pan in a thin layer (about 3 tablespoons), tilting quickly. Cook for 1 to 1.5 minutes until the edges are set and lightly golden, then flip and cook for 30 seconds more. Repeat to make 8 crêpes. Stack and set aside.

Make the suzette sauce: melt the butter and sugar in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook until the sugar caramelises to a light amber. Add the orange juice and zest: it will bubble vigorously. Stir until the caramel dissolves into a smooth sauce.

Fold each crêpe into quarters and add to the sauce. Turn to coat. Add the Grand Marnier and tilt the pan slightly: if you have a gas hob you can let the fumes catch on the flame; otherwise stir and let the alcohol cook off for 1 minute. Serve 2 crêpes per person with a spoonful of sauce, and vanilla ice cream alongside.
